title: Rowing clubs, yacht clubs and Halloween jobs
summary: The Owls played rowing and Southern Yacht Club jobs; Crum refused regular Saturdays because Halloween paid more.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: You got a note here, Dick, for rowing clubs? Yeah, did you ever work for any rowing clubs? Were you in the band when they did that, the Owls?

Yes, we played a couple of jobs for the rowing club there. We used to row that two-mile job along the New Basin Canal. You remember? I remember one of the guys in it was Jacquet. That was his last name because I knew him. Camille. Camille Jacquet. He was the stroke woman over there. And we wanted, the Yacht Club, we played a couple of jobs at the Yacht Club and they wanted to give us a membership and everything else if we'd play two or three given nights, Saturday nights in the year.
Is that the Southern Yacht Club?
They used to do that at the New Orleans Athletic Club, too.

Yeah, well, I know. But Crum figured that, he said, no, he says, you get on a job and they want you to play on a Halloween night. Halloween night used to be a big night back in those days. Oh, really? Yeah, that was one of the big nights of the year. And he says, suppose they want you on Halloween night? He says, they take you off the job, you're with it. And I said, the job, he said, you can't do it. Yeah, you lose five dollars. So.
